title: Gandhi & mass movements
examples: What was the main goal of the Non-Cooperation Movement?
How did the Salt March relate to British rule?
When did the Quit India Movement happen?

explain.say: Today we learn about Gandhi's big movements in India.
The Non-Cooperation Movement asked Indians to withdraw support from British rule.
The Civil Disobedience Movement focused on breaking unjust laws, like the salt tax.
The Quit India Movement demanded that the British leave India immediately.

draw.text: Quit India: Demand for immediate exit

explain.say: In real life, these movements show people uniting for a common goal.
A common mistake is thinking one protest solves everything right away.

faq.q: Why did Gandhi start the Non-Cooperation Movement?
faq.a: Gandhi started it because he felt Indians needed to withdraw support from British rule. This was a way to show their lack of support.
asks: What was the aim of the Non-Cooperation?

faq.q: What was the main focus of the Civil Disobedience Movement?
faq.a: This movement focused on breaking unjust laws, especially those related to salt. It was a direct challenge to unfair rules.
asks: How did the salt tax affect people?

faq.q: What did the Quit India Movement demand?
faq.a: It was a direct and strong demand for the British to leave India immediately. The name itself explains the goal.
asks: When did people demand India's freedom?
What was the final call for independence?

faq.a: Gandhi strongly promoted non-violence, so the movements were largely peaceful protests. However, sometimes things became difficult.

faq.q: What was the significance of the Salt March?
faq.a: The Salt March was a powerful act of civil disobedience against the unfair salt tax. It gained worldwide attention to show the injustice.
asks: Why was salt important for protest?
What did the salt march achieve?

facts: The Non-Cooperation Movement encouraged boycotting British goods and institutions.
The Civil Disobedience Movement was famously highlighted by the Salt March.
The Quit India Movement was a direct demand for British withdrawal from India.
Gandhi championed non-violent resistance throughout these campaigns.

quiz.say: Which movement involved boycotting schools and courts?
quiz.why: This movement specifically called for withdrawing support from British systems.

wrong.0: This movement was a final, direct demand for the British to leave.
wrong.1: The Salt March was a key event within the Civil Disobedience Movement.
wrong.3: This movement focused more on breaking specific laws, not general boycott.

quiz.say: Breaking an unjust law, like the salt tax, is linked to which action?
quiz.why: The core idea of this movement was the peaceful breaking of unfair laws.

wrong.0: This was a demand for the entire country to be left.
wrong.1: Boycott is a tactic, but Civil Disobedience is the overall movement.
wrong.3: This was broader, involving withdrawing support, not just breaking laws.

quiz.say: If the goal was the immediate departure of the British, which movement was it?
quiz.why: The name itself clearly states the demand for the British to leave India.

wrong.1: This movement was about withdrawing support gradually.
wrong.2: This focused on challenging specific, unjust laws.
wrong.3: This was a specific action, not the overarching movement name.
